name: Garlic gel for hair

lead: Garlic gel is a topical preparation containing garlic that researchers tested in patients with patchy hair loss from alopecia areata. In that trial the gel was used on top of a steroid cream, and the aim was to see whether it improved regrowth in bald patches.

Outside clinics, garlic and other natural extracts such as onion juice and rosemary oil circulate on social media as hair-loss remedies. A 2023 review in Cutis examined the evidence behind several of these TikTok trends, including garlic gel. The published human evidence for garlic gel is a single small randomised trial.

paras: In the published trial, patients applied the gel to affected patches twice daily for three months, alongside a betamethasone cream used in both the garlic and placebo groups. Hair counts and the number of terminal hairs were recorded each month. Social-media routines are less standardised and usually involve homemade garlic preparations.

The trial authors reported no complications in the study group. Outside trials, raw garlic is a known skin irritant, and homemade preparations are not standardised. Alopecia areata is a recurrent autoimmune-type condition and has its own medical treatments, so a dermatologist is the usual source of a diagnosis.

chain: Garlic gel applied to bald patches
Studied as an add-on to a steroid cream in alopecia areata
Possible regrowth of hair in patches
angle.text: People look to garlic gel to help regrow hair in patchy alopecia areata. In the one published trial it was applied twice daily for three months along with a steroid cream, and patches were assessed by hair counts.

lead: Garlic gel for hair is a topical gel made with garlic extract that has been tested as an add-on treatment for localized alopecia areata, a recurrent, non-scarring form of hair loss that produces round bald patches[1]. People interested in hair regrowth also mention garlic, onion juice and similar kitchen ingredients as natural options on social media[2].

The appearance link is direct. In alopecia areata, patches of hair are lost from the scalp or other areas, and the goal of any treatment is regrowth that fills those patches back in. The trial that tested garlic gel counted hairs and terminal hairs in treated patches each month[1].

A 2007 randomised, double-blind trial in the Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology and Leprology compared garlic gel with placebo gel, with both groups also using betamethasone valerate cream. Forty patients took part, and the authors reported good or moderate responses in all garlic-treated patients, a significantly better result than in the control group[1]. A 2014 review of randomised controlled trials in alopecia areata lists treatments with less scientific support under a miscellaneous group, and a 2023 review in Cutis looked at garlic gel among topical remedies promoted on TikTok[2][3].
infobox: Not an approved drug; studied in a clinical trial

paras: The documented use is as an adjunct for localized alopecia areata, where it was applied twice daily to patches for three months[1]. On social media, garlic gel and other natural extracts are discussed more broadly as hair-loss remedies[2].

In the 2007 trial, 20 patients received garlic gel and 20 received placebo, and all used betamethasone cream. At the end of three months the garlic group had good or moderate responses in 19 and 1 patients respectively, which the authors reported as significantly better than the control group[1]. Because both groups used the steroid cream, the study tested garlic gel as an addition to it rather than on its own.
The trial authors state that no complication was observed in the garlic group[1].

A 2023 Cutis review examined the evidence behind topical hair-loss remedies popular on TikTok, listing herbs and extracts including rosemary oil, rice water, onion juice and garlic gel[2]. A 2014 review of 29 randomised trials in alopecia areata covered the range of treatments, with a miscellaneous group having less scientific support[3].

A 2007 double-blind randomised controlled study of 40 patients with localized alopecia areata compared garlic gel with placebo, both combined with betamethasone valerate cream, over three months; it reported significantly better regrowth scores with garlic gel[1]. A 2014 trial review and a 2023 review of social-media remedies give wider context[2][3].

timeline.event: A randomised, double-blind trial of garlic gel plus betamethasone cream in localized alopecia areata is published[1].
A review of randomised trials in alopecia areata is published in the American Journal of Clinical Dermatology[3].
Cutis reviews the evidence behind topical hair-loss remedies on TikTok, including garlic gel[2].
